lines.text: Before he was Vivekananda, he was Naren, a boy in Calcutta.
lines.ph: bᵻfˈoːɹ hiː wʌz vɪvˌeɪkɑːnˈʌndə, hiː wˈʌz nəɹˈeɪn, ɐ bˈɔɪ ɪn kælkˈʌɾə.

lines.text: At twilight, his mother would read him the Ramayana and the Mahabharata.
lines.ph: æt twˈaɪlaɪt, hɪz mˈʌðɚ wʊd ɹˈiːd hˌɪm ðə ɹɑːmˈɑːjənə ænd ðˈə məhˌɑːbˈɑːɹətə.

lines.text: His father, Western-educated, handed him a Bible and said: if there is anything called religion, it is in this.
lines.ph: hɪz fˈɑːðɚ, wˈɛstɚnˈɛdʒuːkˌeɪɾᵻd, hˈændᵻd hˌɪm ɐ bˈaɪbəl ænd sˈɛd: ɪf ðɛɹ ɪz ˈɛnɪθˌɪŋ kˈɔːld ɹᵻlˈɪdʒən, ɪɾ ɪz ɪn ðˈɪs.

lines.text: Two worlds, side by side, in one house.
lines.ph: tˈuː wˈɜːldz, sˈaɪd baɪ sˈaɪd, ɪn wˈʌn hˈaʊs.

lines.text: Reading the Gita as a boy, a single great sentence would stop him, and throb through his brain for days and nights.
lines.ph: ɹˈiːdɪŋ ðə ɡˈiːtɑː æz ɐ bˈɔɪ, ɐ sˈɪŋɡəl ɡɹˈeɪt sˈɛntəns wʊd stˈɑːp hˌɪm, ænd θɹˈɑːb θɹuː hɪz bɹˈeɪn fɔːɹ dˈeɪz ænd nˈaɪts.

lines.text: They who find pleasure and pain the same, heat and cold the same, friend and foe the same.
lines.ph: ðeɪ hˌuː fˈaɪnd plˈɛʒɚ ænd pˈeɪn ðə sˈeɪm, hˈiːt ænd kˈoʊld ðə sˈeɪm, fɹˈɛnd ænd fˈoʊ ðə sˈeɪm.

lines.text: And Krishna's words to Arjuna on the battlefield: ill doth it befit thee, Arjuna, to yield to unmanliness.
lines.ph: ˈænd kɹˈɪʃnəz wˈɜːdz tuː ˈɑːɹdʒʊnə ɔnðə bˈæɾəlfˌiːld: ˈɪl dʌθ ɪt bᵻfˈɪt ðˈiː, ˈɑːɹdʒʊnə, tə jˈiːld tʊ ʌnmˈænlinəs.

lines.text: How strong, he said.
lines.ph: hˌaʊ stɹˈɔŋ, hiː sˈɛd.

lines.text: In eighteen eighty-one, at college in Calcutta, John Stuart Mill's Three Essays on Religion upset his boyhood faith.
lines.ph: ɪn ˈeɪtiːn ˈeɪɾiwˌʌn, æt kˈɑːlɪdʒ ɪn kælkˈʌɾə, dʒˈɑːn stˈuːɚt mˈɪlz θɹˈiː ˈɛseɪz ˌɔn ɹᵻlˈɪdʒən ʌpsˈɛt hɪz bˈɔɪhʊd fˈeɪθ.

lines.text: A friend gave him Hume's scepticism, and Herbert Spencer's doctrine of the Unknowable.
lines.ph: ɐ fɹˈɛnd ɡˈeɪv hˌɪm hjˈuːmz skˈɛptɪsˌɪzəm, ænd hˈɜːbɚt spˈɛnsɚz dˈɑːktɹɪn ʌvðɪ ʌnnˈoʊəbəl.

lines.text: He went on to Descartes, Spinoza, Darwin, Comte, and the Germans: Kant, Fichte, Hegel, Schopenhauer.
lines.ph: hiː wɛnt ˈɔn tuː deɪkˈɑːɹt, spɪnˈoʊzə, dˈɑːɹwɪn, kˈoʊnt, ænd ðə dʒˈɜːmənz: kˈɑːnt, fˈɪktə, hˈeɪɡəl, ʃˈoʊpənhaʊɚ.

lines.text: He even attended lectures at the Medical College, to learn how the nerves and the brain work.
lines.ph: hiː ˈiːvən ɐtˈɛndᵻd lˈɛktʃɚz æt ðə mˈɛdɪkəl kˈɑːlɪdʒ, tə lˈɜːn hˌaʊ ðə nˈɜːvz ænd ðə bɹˈeɪn wˈɜːk.

lines.text: What he learned was this. The brain and the senses react to outside stimuli, and only those changes in the mind are ever known.
lines.ph: wˌʌt hiː lˈɜːnd wʌz ðˈɪs. ðə bɹˈeɪn ænd ðə sˈɛnsᵻz ɹɪˈækt tʊ aʊtsˈaɪd stˈɪmjʊlˌaɪ, ænd ˈoʊnli ðoʊz tʃˈeɪndʒᵻz ɪnðə mˈaɪnd ɑːɹ ˈɛvɚ nˈoʊn.

lines.text: What the outer world really is, the thing that causes them, stays unknown and unknowable.
lines.ph: wˌʌt ðɪ ˈaʊɾɚ wˈɜːld ɹˈiəli ɪz, ðə θˈɪŋ ðæt kˈɔːzᵻz ðˌɛm, stˈeɪz ʌnnˈoʊn ænd ʌnnˈoʊəbəl.

lines.text: Inside, it is the same. Some unknown entity makes the mind say I. It too lies beyond time and space.
lines.ph: ɪnsˈaɪd, ɪɾ ɪz ðə sˈeɪm. sˌʌm ʌnnˈoʊn ˈɛntᵻɾi mˌeɪks ðə mˈaɪnd sˈeɪ ˈaɪ. ɪt tˈuː lˈaɪz bᵻjˌɔnd tˈaɪm ænd spˈeɪs.

lines.text: Inward or outward, the mind was kept back by the impregnable wall of time and space.
lines.ph: ˈɪnwɚd ɔːɹ ˈaʊtwɚd, ðə mˈaɪnd wʌz kˈɛpt bˈæk baɪ ðɪ ɪmpɹˈɛɡnəbəl wˈɔːl ʌv tˈaɪm ænd spˈeɪs.

lines.text: Worse, the sense perceptions themselves are full of errors.
lines.ph: wˈɜːs, ðə sˈɛns pɚsˈɛpʃənz ðɛmsˈɛlvz ɑːɹ fˈʊl ʌv ˈɛɹɚz.

lines.text: Look at these two lines. They are exactly the same length.
lines.ph: lˈʊk æt ðiːz tˈuː lˈaɪnz. ðeɪ ɑːɹ ɛɡzˈæktli ðə sˈeɪm lˈɛŋθ.

lines.text: Knowing it does not help. The eye still sees one longer.
lines.ph: nˈoʊɪŋ ɪt dʌznˌɑːt hˈɛlp. ðɪ ˈaɪ stˈɪl sˈiːz wˈʌn lˈɔŋɡɚ.

lines.text: So whom should philosophy trust? The senses of ordinary people, or the rare realisations of a Buddha or a Jesus?
lines.ph: sˌoʊ hˈuːm ʃˌʊd fɪlˈɑːsəfi tɹˈʌst? ðə sˈɛnsᵻz ʌv ˈɔːɹdɪnˌɛɹi pˈiːpəl, ɔːɹ ðə ɹˈɛɹ ɹˌiːələzˈeɪʃənz əvə bˈuːdə ɔːɹ ɐ dʒˈiːzəs?

lines.text: His friend Brajendranath Seal offered him a system: the sovereignty of Universal Reason.
lines.ph: hɪz fɹˈɛnd bɹədʒˈeɪndɹənɑːt sˈiːl ˈɔfɚd hˌɪm ɐ sˈɪstəm: ðə sˈɑːvɚɹˌɪnti ʌv jˌuːnɪvˈɜːsəl ɹˈiːzən.

lines.text: It conquered his intellect. But his heart, he confessed, still belonged to the individual.
lines.ph: ɪt kˈɑːŋkɚd hɪz ˈɪntəlˌɛkt. bˌʌt hɪz hˈɑːɹt, hiː kənfˈɛst, stˈɪl bᵻlˈɔŋd tə ðɪ ˌɪndᵻvˈɪdʒuːəl.

lines.text: A pale, bloodless reason could not save him in the hour of temptation.
lines.ph: ɐ pˈeɪl, blˈʌdləs ɹˈiːzən kʊd nˌɑːt sˈeɪv hˌɪm ɪnðɪ ˈaʊɚɹ ʌv tɛmptˈeɪʃən.

lines.text: He wanted a flesh and blood reality. A hand to save him. A master who embodied perfection.
lines.ph: hiː wˈɔntᵻd ɐ flˈɛʃ ænd blˈʌd ɹɪˈælᵻɾi. ɐ hˈænd tə sˈeɪv hˌɪm. ɐ mˈæstɚ hˌuː ɛmbˈɑːdid pɚfˈɛkʃən.

lines.text: So he went from place to place in Calcutta, hearing big lectures, and asking each lecturer one question.
lines.ph: sˌoʊ hiː wɛnt fɹʌm plˈeɪs tə plˈeɪs ɪn kælkˈʌɾə, hˈɪɹɪŋ bˈɪɡ lˈɛktʃɚz, ænd ˈæskɪŋ ˈiːtʃ lˈɛktʃɚɹɚ wˈʌn kwˈɛstʃən.

lines.text: Have you seen God?
lines.ph: hæv juː sˈiːn ɡˈɑːd?

lines.text: The man would be taken aback at the very idea.
lines.ph: ðə mˈæn wʊd biː tˈeɪkən ɐbˈæk æt ðə vˈɛɹi aɪdˈiə.

lines.text: Only one man said, I have. And I will put you in the way of seeing Him too. That was Ramakrishna.
lines.ph: ˈoʊnli wˈʌn mˈæn sˈɛd, aɪ hˈæv. ænd aɪ wɪl pˌʊt juː ɪnðə wˈeɪ ʌv sˈiːɪŋ hˌɪm tˈuː. ðɐt wˈʌz ɹˌɑːməkɹˈɪʃnə.

lines.text: The philosopher Hamilton had written that the intellect can only hint that God exists.
lines.ph: ðə fɪlˈɑːsəfɚ hˈæməltən hæd ɹˈɪʔn̩ ðætðɪ ˈɪntəlˌɛkt kæn ˈoʊnli hˈɪnt ðæt ɡˈɑːd ɛɡzˈɪsts.

lines.text: It cannot reveal His nature. It comes closer and closer, and never arrives.
lines.ph: ɪt kænˈɑːt ɹᵻvˈiːl hɪz nˈeɪtʃɚ. ɪt kˈʌmz klˈoʊsɚ ænd klˈoʊsɚ, ænd nˈɛvɚɹ ɚɹˈaɪvz.

lines.text: Where philosophy ends, Hamilton said, religion begins.
lines.ph: wˌɛɹ fɪlˈɑːsəfi ˈɛndz, hˈæməltən sˈɛd, ɹᵻlˈɪdʒən bɪɡˈɪnz.

lines.text: Naren loved that line, and quoted it again and again.
lines.ph: nəɹˈeɪn lˈʌvd ðæt lˈaɪn, ænd kwˈoʊɾᵻd ɪɾ ɐɡˈɛn ænd ɐɡˈɛn.

lines.text: Ramakrishna gave him a prayer: O God, I do not know Thy nature. Manifest Thyself to me as Thou really art.
lines.ph: ɹˌɑːməkɹˈɪʃnə ɡˈeɪv hˌɪm ɐ pɹˈɛɹ: ˈoʊ ɡˈɑːd, aɪ duːnˌɑːt nˈoʊ ðˌaɪ nˈeɪtʃɚ. mˈænɪfˌɛst ðaɪsˈɛlf tə mˌiː æz ðˈaʊ ɹˈiəli ˈɑːɹt.

lines.text: Naren gave up every picture of God, even the formless one with attributes.
lines.ph: nəɹˈeɪn ɡˈeɪv ˌʌp ˈɛvɹi pˈɪktʃɚɹ ʌv ɡˈɑːd, ˈiːvən ðə fˈɔːɹmləs wˈʌn wɪð ˈætɹɪbjˌuːts.

lines.text: He removed all thought, and held his mind still, like the flame of a lamp in a windless place.
lines.ph: hiː ɹᵻmˈuːvd ˈɔːl θˈɔːt, ænd hˈɛld hɪz mˈaɪnd stˈɪl, lˈaɪk ðə flˈeɪm əvə lˈæmp ɪn ɐ wˈɪndləs plˈeɪs.

lines.text: At times the sense of time and body vanished. He sat like this whole nights.
lines.ph: æt tˈaɪmz ðə sˈɛns ʌv tˈaɪm ænd bˈɑːdi vˈænɪʃt. hiː sˈæt lˈaɪk ðɪs hˈoʊl nˈaɪts.

lines.text: One night, after meditation, a monk in ochre appeared, filling the room with light, a water pot in his hand.
lines.ph: wˈʌn nˈaɪt, ˈæftɚ mˌɛdɪtˈeɪʃən, ɐ mˈʌŋk ɪn ˈoʊkɚɹ ɐpˈɪɹd, fˈɪlɪŋ ðə ɹˈuːm wɪð lˈaɪt, ɐ wˈɔːɾɚ pˈɑːt ɪn hɪz hˈænd.

lines.text: He walked toward Naren, as if to say something. Seized with fear, Naren got up and left the room.
lines.ph: hiː wˈɔːkt təwˈɔːɹd nəɹˈeɪn, æz ɪf tə sˈeɪ sˈʌmθɪŋ. sˈiːzd wɪð fˈɪɹ, nəɹˈeɪn ɡɑːt ˌʌp ænd lˈɛft ðə ɹˈuːm.

lines.text: When he came back, the monk was gone.
lines.ph: wˌɛn hiː kˈeɪm bˈæk, ðə mˈʌŋk wʌz ɡˈɔn.

lines.text: It may be a hallucination, he said later. But very often it comes to my mind that I saw Lord Buddha that day.
lines.ph: ɪt mˈeɪ biː ɐ hɐlˌuːsᵻnˈeɪʃən, hiː sˈɛd lˈeɪɾɚ. bˌʌt vˈɛɹi ˈɔfən ɪt kˈʌmz tə maɪ mˈaɪnd ðæt aɪ sˈɔː lˈɔːɹd bˈuːdə ðæt dˈeɪ.

lines.text: The doubts did not end in a day. He fought every inch of the way.
lines.ph: ðə dˈaʊts dɪdnˌɑːt ˈɛnd ɪn ɐ dˈeɪ. hiː fˈɔːt ˈɛvɹi ˈɪntʃ ʌvðə wˈeɪ.

lines.text: But slowly a conviction grew. The gods might be false, he thought. But not God.
lines.ph: bˌʌt slˈoʊli ɐ kənvˈɪkʃən ɡɹˈuː. ðə ɡˈɑːdz mˌaɪt biː fˈɔls, hiː θˈɔːt. bˌʌt nˌɑːt ɡˈɑːd.

lines.text: His intellect was not stunted to be silenced. It was taken to its height, and then beyond.
lines.ph: hɪz ˈɪntəlˌɛkt wʌz nˌɑːt stˈʌntᵻd təbi sˈaɪlənst. ɪt wʌz tˈeɪkən tʊ ɪts hˈaɪt, ænd ðˈɛn bᵻjˈɔnd.

lines.text: The student who read Kant would become a monk, and carry Kant's question to the West.
lines.ph: ðə stˈuːdənt hˌuː ɹˈiːd kˈɑːnt wʊd bɪkˌʌm ɐ mˈʌŋk, ænd kˈæɹi kˈɑːnts kwˈɛstʃən tə ðə wˈɛst.
